key_insight: WorldGuide turns video world modeling into a goal-directed, closed-loop process: it doesn’t just predict what might happen next, it adapts each next action based on what it has already generated. This makes long-horizon procedural task execution more reliable than open-loop video generation.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the gap between generating plausible video trajectories and actually completing multi-step tasks. Existing methods struggle to decide the next action from the generated state, execute it, and detect task completion without relying on external executors or indirect checks.
method: Generate a video-based world model that represents the evolving state of the environment.
Use the generated state to choose the next action, then execute it in a closed loop.
Continuously verify progress and determine when the procedural task is complete.
impact: This is useful for AI/ML practitioners building agents that must act over long horizons in changing environments. It moves video generation from passive prediction toward actionable task execution, which is important for robotics, planning, and interactive AI systems.
visual_elements: A loop diagram showing observe → decide → act → verify → repeat
A side-by-side comparison of open-loop vs closed-loop video generation
An icon-based pipeline for state, action, execution, and completion check
A timeline showing task steps with generated frames at each stage
paper_title: WorldGuide: Goal-Directed Video World Model for Procedural Task Execution
paper_authors: Ankan Deria, Komal Kumar, Hisham Cholakkal, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, Salman Khan
